investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-29T18:24–18:31Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes have zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes failing pod affinity/selector matching. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available production nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod VM slots fully consumed), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~146 seconds until the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity or configuration issue scoped to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource slots are fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all peer-pod VM capacity is in use and no preemption victims exist, leaving no room for new agent pods (strongest evidence: scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and 'No preemption victims found')

The 4 remaining nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label or runtime class at all, meaning the pod's node affinity or nodeSelector restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, which are already saturated

A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe runs, causing resource exhaustion that would not occur at normal capacity

The peer-pod provider (cloud VM quota, API rate limit, or provider-side capacity) may be rejecting new VM allocations, causing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on those nodes to report zero available slots even if pods are not actively running

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the eval's remote agent pod because the 2 nodes that support kata.peerpods.io/vm have insufficient VM capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never schedules, the agent is never created, and the eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs never reaches the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for the peer-pod VM required to back a remote agent. The eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), which triggers pod creation; the pod stalls unscheduled for ~147 seconds before the eval times out, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduling error message, latencyMs=150145, evidenceKeys=[] — runtime check also failed at the pod scheduling layer

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1905, which is the call that triggers remote pod creation; failure here prevents all downstream evidence writes
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract at line 264 requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none were produced
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes — concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/stuck pods have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for the eval's probe pod.

Secondary: Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift — the pod's node affinity targets only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and if those nodes were cordoned, drained, or had their labels changed, the effective schedulable pool would be zero even if VM quota remained.

Tertiary: Cluster under-provisioning — the cluster has only 2 nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm support; if baseline workload demand has grown, the eval probe competes with production pods for a small fixed resource pool.

Lower confidence: Transient scheduling spike — a burst of remote agent creation requests at the time of the eval run temporarily exhausted VM slots; capacity may have recovered after the eval window closed.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes cluster shows ample unallocated kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a misconfiguration (e.g., wrong node selector, missing resource request) would need to be investigated instead.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-29T18:24–18:31Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes have zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes failing pod affinity/selector matching. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available production nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod VM slots fully consumed), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~146 seconds until the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity or configuration issue scoped to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

The 4 remaining nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label or runtime class at all, meaning the pod's node affinity or nodeSelector restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, which are already saturated

A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe runs, causing resource exhaustion that would not occur at normal capacity

The peer-pod provider (cloud VM quota, API rate limit, or provider-side capacity) may be rejecting new VM allocations, causing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on those nodes to report zero available slots even if pods are not actively running

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-29T18:26–18:31Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the Swarm pod could not be placed because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received any response evidence, leaving all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~146–147 s), preventing the eval from reaching the runtime stage and producing any evidence. This is a cluster-capacity or node-affinity configuration issue localized to the production-api Kubernetes environment, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is currently scoped to the observability eval.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=150145, confirming the pod sat unscheduled for ~146 s before the eval timed out.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was ever returned, consistent with the pod never starting.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, confirming the runtime stage was never reached.
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=150295, endedAt=2026-06-29T18:26:35 — the same exhaustion condition blocked agent creation ~3 minutes before the runtime check ran.
sibling.remote-agent-state: near-identical scheduler message (147 s), latencyMs=150117, endedAt=2026-06-29T18:29:05 — state polling also failed for the same reason.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) as the first substantive step; a scheduling failure here would prevent all downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false, confirming the severity classification is correct but all three checks are failing.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules restrict scheduling to a subset of nodes that no longer has sufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded entirely by selector mismatch. A recent node label change or pool resize could have reduced the eligible node count.

Tertiary — cluster node pool under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been sized for a lower concurrency level than current demand, and no auto-scaling or preemption policy is configured to recover (preemption: 0/6 nodes available, no victims found).

Lower probability — leaked/stuck remote-agent pods from a previous eval run consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and not being cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1916).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place remote-agent pods due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes and affinity mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes. This blocks all three remote-agents checks.
affectedAreas.details: Evidenced by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state all reporting the identical Unschedulable condition.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe
affectedAreas.reason: The probe at line 1914–1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers the failing pod scheduling. Because the pod never starts, no evidence is collected and the contract validation fails entirely.

affectedAreas.label: Feature registry — remote-agents feature checks
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing. The feature is configured with degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2, meaning two required-check failures (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) already satisfy the outage threshold.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: The contract at line 266–270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message; all five are missing because the pod never started. The message assertion ('hello from aura') was never evaluated.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the Kubernetes cluster for kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes; determine how many slots are allocated vs. available.
Audit running pods for any leaked remote-agent eval pods that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and terminate them if found.

Review the node affinity/selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec to determine whether the 4 currently excluded nodes could be made eligible (e.g., by adding the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource or adjusting labels), which would expand the schedulable pool.
If capacity is genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate scaling up the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool or increasing the VM slot limit on existing nodes.

Confirm whether the remote-agents feature has crossed the outageAfterFailures=2 threshold (remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are both required=true and both failing), and update any status page or alerting accordingly.

Once the scheduling issue is resolved, re-run all three remote-agents checks to verify recovery and confirm the expected-output contract is satisfied (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all present; message contains 'hello from aura').

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval succeeds and returns all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), the scheduling issue has resolved and was transient.

If kubectl or equivalent shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and may instead be a pod spec or affinity misconfiguration.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes are found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the pod's node selector is simply wrong, the root cause shifts to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.
If no remote-agent pods are currently running (i.e., no leaked pods consuming slots), the cause is pure capacity under-provisioning rather than a cleanup failure.
If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks are also failing with scheduling errors, the problem may be broader than the kata.peerpods.io/vm node class alone.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes, alerting before full exhaustion rather than after scheduling failure.

Add a pre-flight eval that verifies at least one node matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector has available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting agent creation, to distinguish capacity exhaustion from affinity misconfiguration.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that checks for remote-agent pods in non-terminal states older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 10 minutes), to catch cleanup failures from the withCleanup wrapper.

Consider adding a historical baseline to the remote-agents checks (verifierContext.history shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null); establishing a passing baseline would enable currentlyRegressedFromPass detection for faster triage in future failures.
